title: Hail the King: Check the Last Defense
summary: Use king support to seal the escape squares, then answer the rook interposition before claiming mate.

nodes.question: The queen has been captured. Is Rh8 really immediate mate?
nodes.explanation: Rf8 can check along the h-file. Kf3 covers g2 and g3, and Black’s queen occupies g1, but the rook on c7 can still block with ...Rh7.

branches.title: Source idea, corrected defense: block and capture
commentary: Begin after ...Rxc7 at 164 seconds, once the queen sacrifice has reduced the diagram to seven pieces. The source illustrates Rh8 but overlooks an interposition.
Rh8+ checks Kh2 along the h-file. It is not mate: the rook on c7 can reach h7. White’s king guards g2 and g3, and Black’s own queen occupies g1.
Rh7 is Black’s only legal reply. It blocks the h-file, buying one move but putting the rook on a square White can capture. This omitted defense is independently supplied.
Rxh7# captures the blocker and restores the h-file check. Kf3 still covers g2 and g3; Qg1 blocks g1, and the distant queen cannot interpose on the h-file. This is actual mate.

branches.title: Independent mistake: check the threat before moving
commentary: Compare a rook move that does not deliver the necessary h-file check. This is an independently chosen mistake.
Rf7 loses with best defense. The move neither checks Kh2 nor removes Black’s queen; White’s mating cage depends on immediate forcing play, not merely keeping a rook active.

exercises.prompt: Why is Rh8 check rather than mate?
exercises.answer: Black’s rook can slide from c7 to h7 and block the check. White must capture that rook before claiming mate.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t the king escape after the final capture?
exercises.answer: Kf3 controls g2 and g3, the h-file is checked by Rh7, and Black’s queen occupies g1.

startContext: Begin after ...Rxc7 in the complete saved 164-second diagram: White Kf3/Rf8 versus Black Kh2/Qg1/Rc7/a3/c5. These two selected seven-piece lines are checked exactly. The earlier eight-piece king walk, Qc7+ offer and king-retreat alternatives remain outside verification scope. The source’s Rh8 mate claim needs the extra ...Rh7/Rxh7 finish.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: The source calls Rh8 immediate checkmate after ...Rxc7.
sourceCorrections.correction: Rh8 is check, but ...Rh7 is a legal and forced rook interposition. Rxh7 then is actual mate. The added defense and capture are independent corrections to the illustrated source idea.
